'''Takei Ōtomonushi no Kami''' (武居大伴主神, historical kana: たけゐおほともぬしのかみ) is a [[Kami|Kami]] associated with local folklore and the [[Suwa Shrine]] in the [[Suwa Region|Suwa region]] of [[Nagano Prefecture|Nagano Prefecture]].

== Overview ==

The deity's name is also written as '''Takei Ōtomo no Kami''', '''Takei Ebisu''', or '''Takei Emishi'''. Additionally, the 'Suwa Shimosha Daihōri Takei Kei Diagram' identifies "Takei Ebisu no Kami" as a distinct deity, considered the child of Takei Ōtomo no Kami.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1185913/45 |title=Suwa Shimosha Daihōri Takei Kei Diagram |publisher=Suwa Historical Collection |date=1938}}</ref>

Takei Ōtomonushi is regarded as one of the original deities of the Suwa region. According to legend, [[Takeminakata|Takeminakata]] (Suwa Myōjin), enshrined at [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa-taisha]], encountered resistance from Takei Ōtomonushi and [[Moreya|Moreya no Kami]]. However, both were defeated and subsequently became vassals of Takeminakata.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/765072/29 |title=Guardian Gods and Takei Ōtomonushi |publisher=Shinano History Collection |date=1910}}</ref> Other versions suggest disputes between Moreya and Takeminakata over entering Suwa.<ref>Yamada Hajime, 'Takei Ōtomonushi as a Vassal,' Suwa Daimyōjin, 1929.</ref>

According to the traditions of [[Tateshina Shrine]] in [[Tateshina, Nagano|Tateshina]], Takei Ōtomonushi surrendered his territory to Takeminakata and ascended Mount Tateshina.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tateshina Shrine|url=http://www.nagano-jinjacho.jp/shibu/03tousin/02kitasaku/2121.htm|access-date=2019-07-25}}</ref>

== Genealogy ==

Takei Ōtomonushi is considered the ancestor of the [[Takei Horibe (Suwa Taisha)]] priestly lineage, which was historically managed by the [[Imai Clan (Suwa)]].<ref>Ōta Ryō, ‘Shinano,’ Isobe Kōyōdō, 1924.</ref>

== Shrines ==

[[File:蛭子社（武居会美酒） - Takei-Ebisu Shrine.jpg|thumb|<center>Ebisu Shrine (Takei Ebisu)</center>]]

* [[Takei Ebisu Shrine]] (Shimosuwa, Suwa District, Nagano Prefecture)

**Located behind the [[Autumn Shrine]] of Suwa Taisha Shimosha. Dedicated to [[Ebisu (mythology)|Ebisu]].

* [[Hiruko Shrine]] (Takei Ebisu) (Suwa City)

**One of the subordinate shrines of Suwa Taisha Kamisha. Includes the ruins of Takei Hata and Takei Castle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Takei Hata Ruins|url=https://suwacitymuseum.jp/nandemo/koumoku/0100/010212.htm}}</ref>

* [[Ōtomo Shrine (Saku)]] (Saku City, Mochizuki)

**Traditionally linked to Takei Ōtomonushi, though evidence is speculative.<ref>‘Saku County Gazetteer,’ 1983.</ref>
